allow_only_metadata_sharing.description: If true, the listing is only available to get the resource metadata. Listing is non subscribable.
allow_only_metadata_sharing.rationale: This flag selects between two listing product types (full-data sharing vs metadata-only), not who may access the shared data — subscriber access is governed separately by IAM on the exchange/listing. Forcing metadata-only platform-wide would disable the resource's core data-sharing function rather than close an access-control gap.

categories.description: Categories of the listing. Up to two categories are allowed.
categories.rationale: An organisational/discovery tag; it does not itself change security behaviour.

data_exchange_id.description: The ID of the data exchange. Must contain only Unicode letters, numbers (0-9), underscores (_). Should not use characters that require URL-escaping, or characters outside of ASCII, spaces.
data_exchange_id.rationale: An identifier for the resource; it does not itself change security behaviour.

delete_commercial.description: If the listing is commercial then this field must be set to true, otherwise a failure is thrown. This acts as a safety guard to avoid deleting commercial listings accidentally.
delete_commercial.rationale: The API blocks deletion of a commercial listing by default unless this field is explicitly set to true — that default failure is the actual safety guard against accidental deletion. A policy should require this stay false or unset, since pre-setting it to true bypasses the built-in confirmation rather than preserving it.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Deletion-blocking flags follow the prevent-destructive-loss archetype: enforcing PREVENT protects against accidental or malicious destruction of the resource, so this is treated as security-relevant.

description.description: Short description of the listing. The description must not contain Unicode non-characters and C0 and C1 control codes except tabs (HT), new lines (LF), carriage returns (CR), and page breaks (FF).
description.rationale: A free-text label with no functional effect on access, exposure, or data protection.

discovery_type.description: Specifies the type of discovery on the discovery page. Cannot be set for a restricted listing. Note that this does not control the visibility of the exchange/listing which is defined by IAM permission. Possible values: ["DISCOVERY_TYPE_PRIVATE", "DISCOVERY_TYPE_PUBLIC"]
discovery_type.rationale: The resource's own description explicitly states this does not control visibility, which is governed separately by IAM permissions. This is a discovery-page preference, not an access control.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name of the listing. The display name must contain only Unicode letters, numbers (0-9), underscores (_), dashes (-), spaces ( ), ampersands (&) and can't start or end with spaces.
display_name.rationale: An identifier/label for the resource; it does not itself change security behaviour.

documentation.rationale: A free-text description with no functional effect on access, exposure, or data protection.

icon.description: Base64 encoded image representing the listing.
icon.rationale: A cosmetic display image; it does not itself change security behaviour.

listing_id.description: The ID of the listing. Must contain only Unicode letters, numbers (0-9), underscores (_). Should not use characters that require URL-escaping, or characters outside of ASCII, spaces.
listing_id.rationale: An identifier for the resource; it does not itself change security behaviour.

location.description: The name of the location this data exchange listing.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

log_linked_dataset_query_user_email.description: If true, subscriber email logging is enabled and all queries on the linked dataset will log the email address of the querying user. Once enabled, this setting cannot be turned off.
log_linked_dataset_query_user_email.rationale: Controls whether subscriber queries against shared data are attributable to an individual user. This is a genuine audit/accountability control for data governance, directly relevant to detecting misuse of shared data.

primary_contact.description: Email or URL of the primary point of contact of the listing.
primary_contact.rationale: Contact information; it does not itself change security behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project determines resource ownership/location, similar to other identifier fields; it is not itself a security control.

request_access.description: Email or URL of the request access of the listing. Subscribers can use this reference to request access.
request_access.rationale: A contact reference for requesting access; it does not itself grant or restrict access.

bigquery_dataset.description: Shared dataset i.e. BigQuery dataset source.

bigquery_dataset.dataset.description: Resource name of the dataset source for this listing. e.g. projects/myproject/datasets/123
bigquery_dataset.dataset.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the BigQuery dataset). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls — the dataset's own security is enforced at its own resource policies.

bigquery_dataset.replica_locations.description: A list of regions where the publisher has created shared dataset replicas.
bigquery_dataset.replica_locations.rationale: Determines which regions hold physical replicas of the shared data. Policy should restrict this to an approved-region whitelist for data residency, consistent with the project's treatment of other location fields.

bigquery_dataset.selected_resources.description: Resource in this dataset that is selectively shared. This field is required for data clean room exchanges.

bigquery_dataset.selected_resources.rout.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the BigQuery routine). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls.

bigquery_dataset.selected_resources.tabl.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the BigQuery table). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls.

data_provider.description: Details of the data provider who owns the source data.

data_provider.name.rationale: An identifier/label for the data provider; it does not itself change security behaviour.

data_provider.primary_contact.description: Email or URL of the data provider.
data_provider.primary_contact.rationale: Contact information; it does not itself change security behaviour.

publisher.description: Details of the publisher who owns the listing and who can share the source data.

publisher.name.rationale: An identifier/label for the publisher; it does not itself change security behaviour.

publisher.primary_contact.description: Email or URL of the listing publisher.
publisher.primary_contact.rationale: Contact information; it does not itself change security behaviour.

pubsub_topic.data_affinity_regions.description:
Region hint on where the data might be published. Data affinity regions are modifiable.
See https://cloud.google.com/about/locations for full listing of possible Cloud regions.
pubsub_topic.data_affinity_regions.rationale: A region-selecting field, structurally similar to bigquery_dataset.replica_locations on the same resource. Even as a non-binding hint, this field signals and influences where data may be published, and should be constrained to an approved region set like any other location field, following the data residency archetype.

pubsub_topic.topic.description: Resource name of the Pub/Sub topic source for this listing. e.g. projects/myproject/topics/topicId
pubsub_topic.topic.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the Pub/Sub topic). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls.

restricted_export_config.description: If set, restricted export configuration will be propagated and enforced on the linked dataset.

restricted_export_config.enabled.rationale: If enabled is false (or not set), restricted export protections are not enforced for the listing. This policy requires restricted_export_config.enabled to be true so restricted export is actively enforced for the listing.

restricted_export_config.restrict_query_.description: If true, restrict export of query result derived from restricted linked dataset table.
restricted_export_config.restrict_query_.rationale: Directly restricts a genuine data-exfiltration path: exporting query results derived from restricted shared data. This is a clear data-protection control complementing restricted_export_config.enabled.
